versos.texto_bv: Enquanto ele falava comigo essas palavras, baixei o rosto e emudeci.
versos.traducao_literal: E em seu falar comigo segundo as palavras, estas, dei o meu rosto à terra e emudeci.
objecoes: Objeção MATERIAL (revisão ER-0019): RAT-1 (ratio 0,65) e a comparação guiada apontam que a BV omite o complemento locativo presente na traducao_literal ("dei o meu rosto à terra") e nas três referências (ARA "abaixei o rosto para a terra", NVIPT "prostrei-me, rosto em terra", NTLH "olhando para o chão"); o mesmo idiomatismo hebraico já aparece em Dan.10.9, onde a própria BV mantém "com o rosto em terra". — evidência: BV atual (10.15): "baixei o rosto e emudeci"; traducao_literal (10.15): "dei o meu rosto à terra e emudeci"; BV (10.9): "caí em sono profundo, com o rosto em terra"; NTLH/ARA/NVIPT (10.15) mantêm a referência ao chão/terra.

kjv.texto: And when he had spoken such words unto me, I set my face toward the ground, and I became dumb.

vizinhos.14: Now I am come to make thee understand what shall befall thy people in the latter days: for yet the vision is for many days.
vizinhos.16: And, behold, one like the similitude of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spake, and said unto him that stood before me, O my lord, by the vision my sorrows are turned upon me, and I have retained no strength.

web.texto: and when he had spoken to me according to these words, I set my face toward the ground, and was mute.

vizinhos.14: Now I have come to make you understand what shall happen to your people in the latter days; for the vision is yet for many days:
vizinhos.16: Behold, one in the likeness of the sons of men touched my lips: then I opened my mouth, and spoke and said to him who stood before me, my lord, by reason of the vision my sorrows are turned on me, and I retain no strength.
